{{Quote|People of Jelucan, today represents both an ending and a beginning. On this day ends your isolation from the greater galaxy. Instead, Jelucan begins a new and glorious future by assuming its rightful place within the Empire!|[[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin|Tarkin]]|<ref name="Lost Stars" />}}
'''Jelucan''' was a [[planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. The planet sided with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the [[Clone Wars]]. During the [[Imperial Era|Age of the Empire]], Jelucan was annexed by the [[Galactic Empire]]. It was the [[homeworld]] of [[Thane Kyrell]] and [[Ciena Ree]], two star-crossed lovers who fought on opposite sides of the [[Galactic Civil War]].

==Description==
Jelucan was a cold and rocky [[mountain]]ous [[planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]],<ref name="Lost Stars" /> situated along the [[Hydian Way]].<ref name="Galaxy Map" /> It was inhabited by [[human]]s and several [[alien]] species. The planet's population was divided into two communities: a community of human valley dwellers known as the [[First Wavers]] who lived in the planet's remote valley and a [[second-wave]] of human and alien settlers who dwelled in urban centers such as [[Valentia]]. The second wavers tended to be more affluent than the valley dwellers and the two communities distrusted each other. The second wavers looked down on the valley dwellers as primitive and superstitious while the valley dwellers regarded the second wavers as avaricious and selfish. Jelucan was also home to the [[Sentience|non-sentient]] [[muunyak]] [[species]], which were commonly used to carry supplies across the rugged terrain.<ref name="Lost Stars" />

One known mineral from the planet was [[Jelucani fogstone]], which was used to sculpt statues.<ref name="Bloodline" /> Ridgecrawlers were also a common form of transport due to the rocky terrain.<ref name="Lost Stars" />

==History==
[[File:Jelucan_First_Wave_Manga.png|thumb|left|First wave of Jelucan settlers' homes]]
Jelucan was settled relatively late in [[The galaxy|galactic]] history, sometime around [[511 BBY]]. The [[First Wavers]] were exiles from another world who refused to break allegiance to their [[king]] and arrived in near total poverty, but managed to survive. About [[161 BBY|350 years later]], a [[second-wave]] of settlers arrived, who established [[mining]] operations on the planet and considered the ways of the initial settlers to be backward. The second-wave of settlers used the profits from their mining operations to become wealthy aristocrats, while the first wave settlers remained largely destitute.<ref name="Lost Stars" />

[[File:Jelucan_Second_Wave_Manga.png|thumb|right|[[Second-wave|Second wave]] of Jelucan settlers' homes]]
During the [[Clone Wars]], Jelucan was part of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], but following its defeat and the end of the war, Jelucan was initially left independent, but was soon [[Annexation of Jelucan|annexed]] by the [[Galactic Empire]] in [[11 BBY]]. Following this, a giant ceremony on the desolate world which was attended by [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin|Tarkin]] himself. During the ceremony, Tarkin befriended two local children, the second-waver noble [[Thane Kyrell]] and the valley-dweller [[Ciena Ree]], and encouraged them to join the [[Imperial Navy]] when they reached maturity. After the ceremony, multiple Imperial ships returned to their [[Star Destroyer]]s in [[orbit]], however a few headed to newly built Imperial facilities on the southern plateaus. Due to the planet's alignment with the Separatists, the Empire only recruited a handful of [[Imperial cadet]]s from Jelucan, preferring the more populous [[Inner Rim Territories|Inner Rim]] worlds.<ref name="Lost Stars" />

[[6 BBY|Five years later]], Imperial-introduced [[ridgecrawler]]s began to replace the native muunyak species as the common mode of [[transport]]. A few years before the [[Battle of Yavin]], Thane and Ciena were accepted into the prestigious [[Royal Imperial Academy]] on [[Coruscant]]; which the two regarded as part of fulfilling their lives' dream of joining the Imperial Navy. The two cadets graduated shortly before the events of the Battle of [[Yavin Prime|Yavin]] and joined the [[Imperial Navy]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]]. Disillusioned with the Empire's brutality, Thane later defected to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]].<ref name="Lost Stars" />

[[File:JelucanPostYavin.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Jelucan during the Imperial era]]
By the time of the Galactic Civil War, Jelucan had become heavily polluted due to the excessive mining by the Empire. The people of Jelucan also began wearing the same attire, making it nearly impossible to tell the difference between first and second wavers. The planet's legislative building was also taken over by the [[Imperial Military]].<ref name="Lost Stars" />

Following the [[Battle of Hoth]], [[Lieutenant Commander]] Ciena Ree returned to her homeworld after her mother [[Verine Ree]] was falsely accused of embezzling funds at the mine she worked. Despite the doctored evidence, Verine was convicted and sentenced to six years of hard labor. During that time, Ciena reunited with her lover Thane and the two made love despite fighting on opposite sides. By the time of the [[Battle of Jakku]], which marked a [[Galactic Concordance|conclusion]] to the Galactic Civil War and a final defeat for the Empire, Jelucan remained under Imperial control, therefore preventing Thane — who incorrectly believed that Ciena had [[Death|perished]] during the [[Battle of Endor|fighting]] at [[Endor]] — from contacting the [[Ree family]] to offer his condolences for their daughter's supposed death. While fighting at [[Jakku]], however, Thane and Ciena once again crossed paths in a reunion where the former forcefully extracted the latter from the [[Star Destroyer]] ''[[Inflictor]]'' before it crashed into the planet's surface.<ref name="Lost Stars" />

During the time of the [[New Republic]], [[Jelucani fogstone]] was used to build a statue of the rebel hero [[Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]] at the [[New Republic senatorial complex]] on [[Hosnian Prime]]. In [[28 ABY]], the statue was destroyed by the [[Amaxine warriors (New Republic Era)|Amaxine warriors]] during the [[Napkin Bombing]].<ref name="Bloodline" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The climate came first; I tried to think of a type of planet that hadn't really been shown onscreen yet, at least in any of the six films. What I came up with was something Himalayan, high up on the mountains, extremely rugged and even harsh but spiritual, too. That said, Jelucan doesn't take much actual cultural inspiration from real Tibetan or Nepalese beliefs or practices—just the general terrain and the overall feel of the place.|Claudia Gray|<ref name="WoW">{{SW|url=news/writers-on-writing-claudia-gray-and-cecil-castellucci|text=Writers on Writing: Claudia Gray and Cecil Castellucci}}</ref>}}
Jelucan first appeared in [[Claudia Gray]]'s [[2015]] novel ''[[Lost Stars]]'', which was part of the ''[[Journey to Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]'' multimedia series.<ref name="Lost Stars" /> The planet was first illustrated in the reference book ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''.<ref name="Galactuc Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref>

When creating Jelucan, Gray thought about a setting that had not yet been shown on screen in [[George Lucas]]' ''Star Wars'' saga—something akin to [[Wikipedia:Tibet|Tibet]] and [[Wikipedia:Nepal|Nepal]] in the [[Wikipedia:Himalayas|Himalayas]], a rough mountainous environment that is also spiritual. The author adopted the natural aesthetics of the Himalayas but only borrowed one cultural element, that being [[Wikipedia:Sky burial|sky burials]], a common practice that has become threatened by "a steep drop in the [[Wikipedia:Vulture|vulture]] populations."<ref name="WoW" /> Gray named the world after the character [[Wikipedia:Jean-Luc Picard|Jean-Luc Picard]] from the [[Wikipedia:Star Trek|''Star Trek'']] franchise. According to Gray, it is one of several ''Star Trek'' easter eggs she had put into her ''Star Wars'' works, and taking out the middle three letters of Jelucan and putting them at the end spelled "Jeanluc."<ref name="Naming">{{WebCite|url=https://www.spreaker.com/user/14420534/episode-67-claudia-gray-talks-princess-o|text=Episode 67 - Claudia Gray talks Princess of Alderaan, Master & Apprentice, Baby Yoda and Jean-Luc Picard|author=[https://www.spreaker.com/show/streamingstarwars Around the Galaxy]|date=2020-05-25|format=[[Wikipedia:Podcast|Podcast]]|archivedate=20220125042837}}</ref>
